General Certificate of Secondary Education ，即普通教育中级证书，相当于我们理解的
"SSAT ) 之后再继续进行两年的A-level的学习，再来进行大学的申请。
由于进入中国的时间较早，很多知名的国际学校、国际班早年办学都是从A-level课程开始

除了和普通高中国际部一样的中式思维之外，普高学生有两个特点其实并不会在海外大学申请
中占优势的:
首先，执行力强但创造力稍弱;
其次，在高考的竞争与鄙视链下，孩子很容易陷入自乍。
他们中很多孩子会喜欢比大小: 比谁的分数更高，谁的活动更有含金量;他们很害怕自己
low，怕写low的文章，怕回答low的问题; 他们总喜欢把一个简单的概念讲的非常复杂，
从而体现自己旁征博引的能力。而这些行为的背后，是孩子骨子里的不够自信。
每个孩子的背后有天资，有家庭教育，也有学校教育，单从不同的教育体系的大概念来讲，确
实是不同的土壤里开出的不同花采。当我们了解了国际教育的本质与内容之后，再回到如何给
孩子做选择这个问题，大家内心是否更加释然了呢?
我们需要把目光更多的放在我们的孩子身上，了解他的性格特点，他的个人意愿。我的孩
子是擅长执行还是创造力爆棚?他是内向的还是外向的他有过人的才华还是很能考试?
他是否成熟独立?
https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/tDmC6jfj1gLEPpC6knZKPw                                     17/21

题，你自然就能做出明智的抉择了。

Principles used in creating the IB Examination Schedule
1. It is not possible to take into account public, national or school holidays, or religious festivals because of the
number of countries in which the IB Diploma Programme is offered.
2. Registration data has been used to ensure that the minimum number of candidates globally are impacted by
subject timetable clashes.
3. Studies in language and literature and Language acquisition subjects are not scheduled on the same day so a
candidate does not have to be examined in two different language subjects on the same day.
4. Where there are subjects with particular regional or cultural links we will endeavour to take these into account,
for example Arabic literature/language examinations will not be scheduled on a Friday.
5. Almost all subjects are scheduled in an afternoon and morning pattern on consecutive days. This is to minimise
the impact of absence on any given day, whilst maintaining continuity for candidates.
6. Subjects with the highest candidature are not scheduled consecutively and are spread as evenly as possible
over 3 weeks to try and distribute the workload for candidates. Language examinations and science
examinations are scheduled on each of the 3 weeks for the same reason.
7. Except for English, Spanish and French, Language A examinations are scheduled separately from Language B.
8. The examination period remains three weeks long. This is to maintain an acceptable balance between the
number of conflicts in the schedule, the school overheads in running an examination schedule, the time
available to teach, and the IBs responsibility to get the marking done on time to the required quality.
Rescheduling Policy
Rescheduling of an exam for a candidate requires approval from IB.
The criteria and the process for applying for a reschedule can be found in the Diploma Programme Assessment
procedures (formerly Handbook of procedures)
2022 Examination Schedule
The exam schedule in 2022 will start on Thursday 28 April 2022, and end on Friday 20 May 2022, subject to
confirmation in 2021.

guage B course, students further develop their ability to communi-

well as individual written and oral productions. At the end of the
second year, students will sit the externally assessed IB exams.

student is expected to develop in the receptive, productive and

The SAS Chinese Program
The goal of the Chinese program is to enable students to
advocate for self, others and ideas in Chinese in a way that
fosters collaboration, enhances global citizenship, challenges
established thought, and leads to creative ideas. The SAS Chi-
nese program marks progress toward achievement of this goal
through ACTFL standards.
Oral Language
The ability to communicate in oral language is measured
through assessments rooted in the Oral Proficiency Interview
(OPI) by ACTFL. The OPI measures the language proficiency
needed to ensure work readiness for differing types of employ-
ment. The OPI assessment measures from Novice (emerging
levels of language for a young child or second language learn-
er) to Superior (proficiency that provides a linguistic base for
success in careers such as that of a judge, philosopher, or dip-
lomat). The SAS measure of oral language proficiency ranges
from Novice to Advanced High. Advanced High includes most
aspects of the Superior range skills of the OPI.
Literacy
Reading comprehension for class placement is measured
through Level Chinese assessments. Level Chinese offers
assessment as well as support for reading from Level C, a very
basic text of foundational literacy to Level T, which provides
the foundation for Advanced High levels of courses as well as
for the IB Language A courses. Writing samples are analyzed
by teachers. Writing levels range from entrance to the Novice
course, in which students will begin to understand how charac-
ters are formed to the Advanced High course in which students
narrate and persuade with organized, precise and artistically
written language.
Placement
Students are placed in courses that best represent their skill
set and next steps for learning in accordance with standards.
The High School program at SAS offers seven levels of Chi-
nese. The SAS course names reflect the ACTFL exit standard of
the course.

Dance is a course designed for any male or female who would like
to use the assets of dance to improve physical fitness, to increase
talents in athletics, and to develop the ability to dance either for
fun or as a performer. This course combines dance exercises,
dance technique, and dance choreography. The class is designed
to improve posture, strength, flexibility, endurance, agility, balance,
and choreographic and improvisational techniques. Students
will experience various types of dance including ballet, modern,
jazz, hip-hop, Broadway, and some elements of tap, social, and
folk dance and they will incorporate what they have learned into
creative dance choreography. Students will also learn to evaluate
dance and make aesthetic decisions in regards to creativity.
Students will apply appropriate injury prevention techniques and
willlearn aspects of dance history as well. Students can take this
class as a Performing Arts elective (grades 912) or as a Physical
Education elective (grades 1112).

Physical Computing
Course Code: HS7018
Duration: Year
Prerequisites: None
Credits: 1.0
Physical computing refers to the creation of devices that utilize
electronics, mechanical components and computer logic to sense
and respond to the surrounding world. This year-long course is
designed around hands-on activities and projects that challenge
students to design, build and test solutions to authentic problems.
Students will gain experience in a variety of tools of the Maker
Space, programming microcontrollers (e.g. Arduinos), and using a
design process. They will not demonstrate their learning through
exams, but rather through their products and the processes they
use to develop them. They will learn not only how to make things,
but to consider who they design for and why making is worthwhile.
Over the course of the year students will be empowered to develop
their own projects based on questions that interest them. No
previous experience is required or expected.

This two-year course aims to introduce students to some of the
scientific components that make up the study of sport, exercise,
andhealth. The diploma program course in Sports, Exercise, and
Health Science involves the study of the science that underpins
physical performance and provides the opportunity to apply these
principles.
As stated in the IB guide, this course incorporates the traditional
disciplines of anatomy and physiology, biomechanics, psychology,
and nutrition, which are studied in the context of sport, exercise,
and health. Students will cover both core and option topics and
carry out practical (experimental) investigations in both laboratory
and field settings. This will provide an opportunity to acquire the
knowledge and understanding necessary to apply scientific prin-
ciples and critically analyze human performance. Where relevant,
the course will address issues of internationalism and ethics by
considering sport, exercise, and health relative to the individual
and in a global context.
Higher Level Coursework: Students at HL are required to study
additional higher level (AHL) material, conduct extra hours in the
lab, and cover further HL topics within the options. The distinction
between SL and HL is one of breadth and depth. Additional units
include further anatomy; the endocrine system; fatigue; friction
and drag; skill acquisition and analysis; genetics and athletic per-
formance, and exercise and immunity.

English as an Additional Language (EAL) at Shanghai American School
Our students come from a variety of language backgrounds. Some may need support in building academic English proficiency which will
be determined through language proficiency testing and a review of previous school records. All students, however, are immersed in a
rigorous college-preparatory academic curriculum.
SAS is committed to additive bilingualism (maintaining home languages while developing English language proficiency). It is our expecta-
tion that our EAL students will successfully participate in the SAS learning community, have complete access to our entire curriculum,
experience fully the social benefits of being with their peers, and also receive support specific to their language acquisition needs.
EAL Support
Students will have a certified EAL teacher available to support them during general supervised study hall.
EAL Plus (EAL+) Support
Ninth grade students who are identified as needing more support (called EAL +) will receive EAL support during their English 9 and Asian
History courses. English 9 is taught in a sheltered immersion model. A certified EAL teacher will work with the subject teachers in Asian
history. Students will also have a certified EAL teacher available to them during general supervised study hall.

SAS students in grades 11 and 12 may request to take an online course from the Virtual High School (VHS) for SAS credit. These courses will
be taken entirely online from a non-SAS teacher. Courses offered by VHS include AP and regular courses. Many VHS courses are offered
for one semester while AP classes are offered for a full year. You can peruse the courses available in the VHS Course Catalog at http://www.
govhs.org/Pages/Academics-Catalog.
SAS students may take a maximum of seven courses in any semester, which can include one VHS course per semester. The grade for the VHS
course will appear on the students SAS report card and transcript and will be calculated as part of their grade point average. There is no
additional cost for an approved SAS student to take a VHS course.
Students who are interested in taking a VHS course should review all the relevant information on the Virtual High School site and complete
the VHS Pre-Student Survey (http://www.govhs.org/Content/InfoFor-StudentSurvey) to decide if an online course is right for them. Students
should then meet with their guidance counselor to discuss the implications of taking a VHS course.
Students who, after meeting with their counselor, would like to request to take an online VHS course should complete the VHS application
form (available in the Counseling Office) and attach a copy of the VHS Pre-Student Survey with their answers. The completed application
should be submitted to the students counselor with their course selection form at the regular due date for course selections.
Seats for VHS courses are limited. Mr. Tracie Dotson, Puxi HS VHS site coordinator, will make the final approval for all VHS course requests.
Priority for VHS courses will be given to students with schedule conflicts.
If you are interested in taking an online course, please review the VHS Course Catalog (http://www.govhs.org/Pages/Academics-Catalog)
and carefully decide which courses you might like to take. If you have any questions about the VHS program at SAS, please contact your
counselor.

举目四周千山绿，满眼皆是三月喜。 又是一年的努力与拼搏迎来如期而至的收获。截至
2018年4月1日不完全统计，星校第二届全体毕业生93人中近一半同学收获了至少一个美
国综合排名前三十或同等水平的offer，其中包括芝加哥大学，牛津大学，西北大学，范
德堡大学，华盛顿大学圣路易斯分校，埃默里大学，加州大学伯克利分校，加州大学洛杉
矶分校，南加州大学，卡内基梅隆大学，弗吉尼亚大学，塔夫茨大学，维克森林大学，北
卡大学教堂山分校，纽约大学，帝国理工学院在内的顶尖大学学府。93人100%收获至
少一个美国综合排名前六十或同等水平的offer。
在星校第一届毕业生取得可喜成绩的基础上，18届的毕业生的申请有了新的动向并取得
了多重突破。一是在选校和专业的定位上更加精准，超过一半的学生选择了早申
（ED/EA）并收获满意offer，并不再将主要精力放在常规申请（RD）中；二是在地域的
选择上有少部分学生尝试了英国方向的申请，获得了包括牛津大学，帝国理工学院，伦敦
大学学院等诸多英国顶尖名校的offer；三是学生在offer的最终选择上更基于对专业发
展，学术声誉，地理位置等因素的综合判断，不拘泥于排名且不追求offer的绝对数量。
这些和星校一直以来的理念是相符的，因此我们决定公布目前每一位学生可能的去向作
为我们今年申请季的总结。

士校友名录。课间时，倚窗吹着晨风，不远处图书馆和科学馆上两位"两弹元勋"校友题字透过
薄雾在阳光中闪烁。城市的喧嚣被隔绝在校园外，剩下的只有南开独有的厚重历史感与学习
氛围。
不久，偶然在图书馆翻到了一本蒙灰的南开历史文集，试着随便读了读，开篇竟是张伯苓
校长对校训的亲自解释: 略显隐涩的前半句,人允公允能强调自我提升与奉献社会; 而后半
句,日新月异，虽然易懂，但最难做到，代表着自省，以及对未知的勇敢探索。虽然早在入
校时就知道了校训，但于我它终究只是平平常常的八个字，还没认真瞧过。这篇不起眼的简
略校训释义，却给了我从未有过的心灵共鸣。
进入国际部后，每天面对的都是从未接触的全新模式: 大比例英语教学，眼花引乱的选修
课程;眼前未知的恐惧让我感到迷茫不知所措。八字校训中对冲破舒适区，探索未知的鼓
励，恰好是解决我目前困境的不二法门。
这之后，校训成了我名副其实的座右铭，激励着我探索以往从未涉足的方方面面。

生物党好君一起创立了视责体生物小组。利用假期与课后的时间，我们一起在校内以及校外开展了一系列微生物实验，第一次体验了我们共同的梦想职业生涯。具体的实验操作外，我们还一起规划执行了两次完整
的调查统计实验，分析了社区居民对微生物类传染病，以及新冠肺炎的防范意识。进行两次
较大规模实验时，必须保证每个步骤都分毫不差: 仅仅一个污染的培养四都可能使最终数据
可信度惨不忍睹。对于我们这些新手来说，操作绝不轻松，但随之而来的新鲜感却吸引着每
位成员全力以赴。团队合作与计划制定从未显得如此重要，各位同学的特长与想法在交流中
碰撞融合，带来了大家的创造力提升。三年间，我们的小组保持活力，成员们持续分享实验
机会和活动构思; 这样长的时间跨度让视菌体小组在年级中脱颖而出，也帮助我在申请季中
展现对专业的投入与执着。

Do I have to take English?
All students must study English every year. You should decide which type of English
you want to study, based on your level and other commitments. If you have chosen a
wide range of AP courses, you might want to choose Pre-AP English rather than AP
English, as it will be easier for you to manage the work and get a good grade.
Remember that AP means college level, and that AP English is designed for native
speakers. If your English is not exceptionally strong you will struggle with AP English
are likely get a low grade. Pre-AP English would be a better choice, as it would
enable you to build up your overall English skills, including writing, speaking,
grammar and vocabulary, before you attempt AP level English. Remember that in
order to graduate, you must take and pass English in each grade level. This is
another reason you should make sure you do not attempt an English course which is
too difficult for you.
How many courses should I choose?
In addition to English, you should choose 2-3 other course units. One unit is equal
to one full year of study (4-6 hours per week). Most courses are one unit. The
exceptions are Physics C: Mechanics and Physics C: E&M, which are both 0.5 unit
courses. You can choose a maximum of two AP Social Science units each year, two
AP Science units each year (remember that Physics C courses are 0.5 unit courses),
and two AP Math units each year. Although it is common in US high school to take a
math class every year, it is not necessary at this school, and you could choose to do
AP math in only one of your two years. The math you do in Year 1 is very high level,
as is AP math. Many colleges (e.g. UC) consider a score of 3 on AP Calculus AB to
be equal to 3 years of high school math.
Do I really need to take Science and Social Science classes?
In order to graduate you will also need to pass at least one AP course from each of
the subject areas (AP Social Science, AP Science, and AP Math) during your time in
the school. This is in addition to passing English in each grade level. You do not,
however, need to pass a subject from all of these areas in one year: over two years is
fine. This is most important for students progressing to Year 12: make sure you have
taken a course in AP Social Science, AP Science, and AP Math during your time in
the school. If you are not confident (or interested) in a particular area, it might be
better to leave it to Year 12 to give yourself more time to prepare.
What are the entry requirements for different courses?
AP courses are very demanding, and each one has different demands (e.g. some
need high level of English, others need high level of math). As a result, most courses
have entry requirements which must be met in order to ensure you are able to cope
with the demands of the course. There are also some other restrictions which apply.
Details are given below. Note that grade requirements are for semester 1 grades, as
these are the only completed grades you have when registering for courses.

What are the regulations for adding a course?
It is extremely important, for planning and teacher recruitment purposes, for students
to make appropriate course selections. For this reason, the school invests a lot of
hours into checking students selections, both number and type, to make sure these
are appropriate. If you do wish to add a course after the registration deadline, this
cannot be guaranteed, and adding the course will depend on a number of factors,
including the number of students already enrolled in the course and your other course
selections. It can only be done within the first week of the course. You should use
the form in Appendix 4 to make this request.
What are the regulations for dropping a course?
As with adding a course, it is difficult for planning reasons if too many students drop
courses. We do not encourage students to just have a try and drop a course later:
you should register for the correct courses in the first instance. There may, however,
be important reasons for you to drop a course, e.g. too much work or personal
29
reasons. If you do need to drop a course, this is fine, as long as it is done within the
first two weeks of the course. After the two week period it is still possible to drop a
course, but the course will remain in your record, and will show on your transcript.
As the course is incomplete, there will be no credit. There will also be no grade. The
transcript will show WP for Withdrawn Passing or WF for Withdrawn Failing,
depending on your status when you dropped the course. If you wish to drop a course,
either during the first two weeks or later, you should complete the form in Appendix 4
so that records are updated.
How does attending summer school affect my course registration?
HFI recognizes that many students wish to attend a summer school programme.
Students are not encouraged to miss any school time to attend such programmes,
and a calendar is issued very early (usually in January) for appropriate planning.
However, they may be exceptional occasions when students need to miss one or
more days at the start of the academic year because of summer school participation.
In this case, you must notify the Principal directly before mid-May. Notification
must include full and clear documentation of the reason for arriving late, including:
exact dates of summer school;
date you will be coming back to HFI (you must arrive back at school as soon as
is feasible).
You must contact teachers of your courses prior to leaving school for the summer to
be clear on summer assignments and other work.
You must complete the summer assignment for each class and send to teachers one
week before the start of the school year. Teachers may also assign other work,
which you must complete.
Students who are absent on the first day of school and who meet the above
requirements will retain priority for classes for which they are registered.
Students who do not meet these requirements may lose their place in a class to any
students on the waiting list.
Note that if you miss whole first week of school, you lose the option to add any
classes, and will only be able to drop. Also note that absences for summer school in
the first week will be excused, but will count towards the attendance policy. Absences
in the second week will be unexcused.

Do I have to take English?
All students must study English every year. You should decide which type of English
you want to study, based on your level and other commitments. If you have chosen a
wide range of AP courses, you might want to choose Pre-AP English rather than AP
English, as it will be easier for you to manage the work and get a good grade.
Remember that AP means college level, and that AP English is designed for native
speakers. If your English is not exceptionally strong you will struggle with AP English
are likely get a low grade. Pre-AP English would be a better choice, as it would
enable you to build up your overall English skills, including writing, speaking,
grammar and vocabulary, before you attempt AP level English. Remember that in
order to graduate, you must take and pass English in each grade level. This is
another reason you should make sure you do not attempt an English course which is
too difficult for you.
How many courses should I choose?
In addition to English, you should choose 2-3 other course units. One unit is equal
to one full year of study (4-6 hours per week). Most courses are one unit. The
exceptions are Physics C: Mechanics and Physics C: E&M, which are both 0.5 unit
courses. You can choose a maximum of two AP Social Science units each year, two
AP Science units each year (remember that Physics C courses are 0.5 unit courses),
and two AP Math units each year. Although it is common in US high school to take a
math class every year, it is not necessary at this school, and you could choose to do
AP math in only one of your two years. The math you do in Year 1 is very high level,
as is AP math. Many colleges (e.g. UC) consider a score of 3 on AP Calculus AB to
be equal to 3 years of high school math.

however, need to pass a subject from all of these areas in one year: over two years is

taken a course in AP Social Science, AP Science, and AP Math during your time in
the school. If you are not confident (or interested) in a particular area, it might be

When you are promoted to Year 11 or 12, you will need to choose which courses you
want to study. This can be a difficult task. To help you make your decision the school
has planned a series of activities, with information from varies members of the school
(principal, department heads, teachers, college counselors) at different times in the
process. The process, and these activities, are described in more detail below.
Course registration process
The whole process of choosing and registering for courses takes several weeks.
Exact dates will vary from year to year. The stages are as shown below, and
explained in more detail later in this section. For exact dates, see Appendix 2.
Parents meeting
Student meeting about courses
Email about registration
Consult teachers
Registration opens
Registration closes
School reviews choices
School confirms choices
Deadline for fees

There will be a parents meeting each year around this time. This meeting will give
information to your parents about the courses offered by the school, as well as an
overview of the registration process. Although presentations at this meeting will not
be as detailed as the one for students, it will still provide a good chance to get more
information. It will be delivered bilingually, i.e. in English and Chinese, which will help
with clarity. It is also when your parents are likely to be included in the process, and
advice from them will be an important part of your course selection.

The will be presentations about the course registration process and information about
courses. This is a chance for you to understand the whole process, as well as the
course information and the differences between the different subjects. The
presentations will be delivered by the academic staff, in other words, the principal, the
AP department heads, and AP teachers. This is an excellent chance to hear about
your courses from the teachers who will be teaching you next year.

Before the course registration opens, you will be sent an email about the course
registration. The email will give details about how to register and the deadlines.
24

The AP teachers who teach Year 11 and 12 classes will be available for consultation
so you can get a better idea about courses. The school will usually arrange a
consultation session, at which you can meet all of the AP teachers currently in the
school, and have a chance to talk to them individually. Although you may not know
these teachers, they are a valuable resource and you should try to discuss courses
with them if you have questions. It will also give them a good chance to get to know
some of their future students.

The course registration will be conducted using SurveyMonkey. The link to the survey
will be issued via email.

Once the registration closes, you will no longer be able to update your choices. If you
need to make changes after this time, please discuss with College Counseling Dept.
Please note, however, that it may not be possible to change, e.g. if some courses are
full. Make sure you make the correct choices before the registration closes.

Once the registration is closed, the school will begin to review the choices. Once both
Year 11 and Year 10 students have registered, it will be clear what classes still have
spaces, and this information will be shared so that students can add classes or make
changes. This will be handled separately. During this time, you might be given an
appointment with a College Counselor to discuss your course choices, especially if
the school feels there might be a problem. This will give you a further chance to
discuss your course choices, explain reasons for choosing them, and understand
whether or not you have made the right selection.
The school will confirm course choices once the above processes have taken place.

The final stage of the process is payment of fees for course registration and books.
The deadline will normally be one week after the school has confirmed all course
choices. It is important that you make fee payments on time. If you do not, the place
on your courses will no longer be guaranteed and may be offered to other students.

more days at the start of the academic year because of summer school participation.
In this case, you must notify the Principal directly before mid-May. Notification
must include full and clear documentation of the reason for arriving late, including:
exact dates of summer school;
date you will be coming back to HFI (you must arrive back at school as soon as
is feasible).
You must contact teachers of your courses prior to leaving school for the summer to
be clear on summer assignments and other work.
You must complete the summer assignment for each class and send to teachers one
week before the start of the school year. Teachers may also assign other work,
which you must complete.
Students who are absent on the first day of school and who meet the above
requirements will retain priority for classes for which they are registered.
31
Students who do not meet these requirements may lose their place in a class to any
students on the waiting list.
Note that if you miss whole first week of school, you lose the option to add any
classes, and will only be able to drop. Also note that absences for summer school in
the first week will be excused, but will count towards the attendance policy. Absences
in the second week will be unexcused.

【日常学习】Matt有时会布置和读书相关的project，建议自己提前进行读书规
划，不要把任务都挤在ddl前做。
【课前预习】Matt每天都会提前将本节课的handout和需要阅读的课本页数发在
微信群上，担心自己上课跟不上节奏的同学们可以提前略读。
【课堂参与】Matt上课时基本说的每一句话都与文本内容有关，认真听完全程
会觉得很有帮助。他上课时偶尔会有带大家朗读文章的环节，其中会给主动朗
读的同学给予extra credit，想要获得extra credit的同学可以积极参与。
【课后作业】一般作业是阅读课上剩下的内容，读完后需要回答文本后面的问
题。Matt认为作业十分重要，如果没有完成的话会被请出教室，还会影响到日
常的表现分（日常表现分算是Summative分数）。除此之外，作业还有AP
Classroom的练习和需要发送在Formative微信群的作业。
【考前复习】考前Matt会给一份Study Guide，建议自己准备完Study Guide上
的内容后再找他过一遍。
其他
【上课设备】AP Literature课程中大部分时间需要使用平板和触控笔，平板中需
要下载Notability或者Good Notes这两款笔记软件。Matt极少发纸质handout，
所以需要在软件中设立好文件夹分类以归纳各种资料。
【课程工作量】AP Lit因为本身难度的原因，无论是课上还是课下的工作量都是
比较大的。虽然单独记sum的projects是每月一次，但如果算上中间穿插的每周
一次的Progress Check、课上的quick writes、课后的one-paragraph writing、
Level Analysis、每节课要求提前阅读的materials 还有每周的assigned readings，
有时候会让人应接不暇。如果你有充足的耐心和毅力，你一定会在日复一日的
劳作中收获更多。

AP Environmental Science其实是一个结合科学和 social science 的学科，结合生
物、化学物理、地质学、 public policy、public health、economics、politics 等
等。
以下内容来自 College Board:
In a world plagued with problems of global warming, pollution, plastic wastes, and
habitat disruption, studying Environmental Science plays a vital role in understanding the
world we live in and how one can put scientific knowledge and skills in finding solutions
to save the Earth. Students will not just deal with basic facts in Biology with regards to
Ecology rather they will be driven to think critically and connect concepts in Chemistry,
Earth Science, Economics, and Policy making to draft practical solutions for the current
environmental problems.
The goal of the AP Environmental Science course is to provide students with the
scientific principles, concepts, and methodologies required to understand the
interrelationships of the natural world, to identify and analyse environmental problems
both natural and human-made, to evaluate the relative risks associated with these
problems, and to examine alternative solutions for resolving or preventing them. The
course includes methods for analysing and interpreting information and experimental
data, including mathematical calculations.

content:
重要发展、重要进程等。
在世界历史的学习过程中，大家会接触到6个主要的Theme （SPICES），这门
课程的所有知识以及问题都是围绕着这些Theme展开的，它们分别是：Social,
Political, Interaction, Cultural, Economic, Science。提前熟悉这些Theme会让你在
学习世史的过程中更加organized。
此外，世界史和很多其他AP 历史课程一样会要求学生写argumentative essay
（在考试中体现为Long Essay Question & Document Based Question）。所以在课
程中大家也会学习使用历史学家的研究方法分析一手和二手资料 (analyzing
primary and secondary sources)、阐述历史背景 (contextualization)、提出历史性论
点 (developing historical arguments)、发掘不同历史事件之间的关联性 (making
historical connections)、运用逻辑思维来分析历史事件之间的异同、因果关系、
延续及变化 (utilizing reasoning about comparison, causation, and continuity and
change over time)等。
世界史与其他历史类AP课程最大的不同在于它从 global perspective着手。除去
涵盖近一千年几乎所有全球重要历史事件所造就的恢弘的时间横向跨度，世史
的全球性也赋予其无与伦比的历史纵深度。世史所侧重的connections不仅是一

个particular region里的不同时段的发展比较，还有同一时段世界上不同地区之
间的关联和互动。世界史强调的这种宏大而全面的世界视角和思维习惯为大家
提供受益终身的独立思考和发掘关联性的思维能力。

除日常作业之外，每个学期只有一次 final考试。Final一般而言包括听说读
写四个部分，难度会比课时练习稍简单，但具体考试内容与难度会稍微浮动。考
试形式有选择和填空题。口语科目应该是单独的时间测试，其他都是与全校其他
各科的 final同步进行。
除了学业考核之外，应当注意的是出勤率的要求。根据校规，每学期只能有
2次缺勤，否则会面临整门课被 fail的风险。考虑到二外占用了晚自习较长的时
间，如果遇到 sum前一晚上课的情况，应该合理利用请假规则，但是也要控制次
数噢。
二外作为一门语言课程很注重前后衔接和积累，所以能多背单词、多复习的话
对于学习和使用德语会很有帮助。

【2020申请故事】南加和佐治亚理双料offer学姐Alice：不会弹钢琴的辩不是好学霸
朴朴君 浑朴Catalyst 2020-06-09
幸亏我遇了浑朴要不然我真的不知道我的申请会是什么样，可能就不会去做学术活动，也不会去做其他的那些课外活动，书可能也不会
被可爱的Mark改的这么好。
—— Alice
01：个情况
今年申请中，浑朴学员Alice收到了阵offer，分别来南加州学、佐治亚理学院、加州学圣芭芭拉分校、加州学尔湾分校、
加州学圣地亚哥分校、加州学戴维斯分校！
Alice来岛博格思加州学校，她成绩优异、多才多艺、阳光向上，还积极参加学校的各项活动，打过辩论、做过演讲、参与志愿活
动，钢琴演奏更是屈指。（个情况为编辑整理）
02：迷茫中结识浑朴指明灯
https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/PSH0Axr9zkjMX7IsXbfJxA 1/12
我在申请季的时候曾经有段时间常的迷茫，要不是因为遇了浑朴，我也不知道现在的申请会是什么样。
我专业兴趣常多，当时感觉看到什么课都觉得很有趣，什么专业都想去学学，兴趣上其实很多，有时候会去踢球有时候去打辩论，
但总之活动以及兴趣常散，没有任何个集中的向让我去扎实地做学术研究。
我第次接触浑朴是因为我去问Jerry同学关于留学机构的问题，然后他把Carrie师的微信推给了我。Carrie师聊的时候很nice，
我还没有跟浑朴签约，她就已经很真诚地敞开扉，从众多眼花缭乱的活动信息流中，快速匹配了适合我的活动。其专业度和信息敏感
度可斑。
我爸爸妈妈当时在岛和上海都找了家机构，也帮我打听了很多很多，最后确定了浑朴。
迷茫期间，Yicen直跟我通话并且给我提出些活动的点,如说画画或者其他物理相关的。当时在浑朴brainstorming

我爸爸妈妈当时在岛和上海都找了家机构，也帮我打听了很多很多，最后确定了浑朴。迷茫期间，Yicen直跟我通话并且给我提出些活动的点,如说画画或者其他物理相关的。当时在浑朴brainstorming
activities（编者译：头脑暴活动）的时候，我就在想我有什么activities可以写在学申请的那个表单上。我当时想的常常的
多，因为我确实也做过很多很杂的活动，但是常没有向性，这时候Yicen帮我找到了我最闪亮的活动在于物理，所以我们之后就规划
着朝物理这个向的活动继续做下去。
在浑朴帮我找到专业定位以后，他们帮我推荐了个的活动。个就是Pioneer Academics（编者注：研究型夏校），我知道浑
朴的上届学Jerry同学他当时也在做这个项，并且后续取得了个很好的成绩，所以我当时看到这个项以后也想去参加下。
https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/PSH0Axr9zkjMX7IsXbfJxA 2/12
Alice在夏校  Arduino的个板
03：吹波Mark和Xinxin师
我的书师可以说是世界上最强的聆听者，因为我在跟他讨论书的时候他总是能不断地聆听，然后让我说出些我常中不会说出
的点，些偶尔脑闪过的些点他都会记下来，并且带着我引导我在这个点上去发展出篇很棒的书。
我真的是太爱我的书师了，前段时间我拿到USC（南加州学）的offer的时候，Mark还在背后打听问我是不是真的喜欢这个学
校。
我的主书第次是以篇记的形式呈现出来的，然后我它去做了早申，之后我觉得其实内容有些散，因为它确实法体现个更
中的思想，所以我问了Mark可不可以再改篇ideas更加集中的篇书，他也愿意去帮我。
概在份，我和Mark开始了写书的前期准备。我们当时也是在不停地brainstorm，我给他写过去很多的稿，开始都是些碎
碎念，Mark很有耐地全盘接收，在我看来他并不是只是个书师，是像个想要去真正了解你的。最神奇的点是他简直像

Mark开始了写书的前期准备。我们当时也是在不停地brainstorm，我给他写过去很多的稿，开始都是些碎碎念，Mark很有耐地全盘接收，在我看来他并不是只是个书师，是像个想要去真正了解你的。最神奇的点是他简直像
只海豚样永远都不睡觉似的，我有时候凌晨三点改完篇书发给他，他直接就秒回，我就问他你不睡觉吗，然后他说他还在
work。
准备完主书以后就正式开始了申请季最忙的部分，这个时候就要填很多表，如准备财务证明。在这提个的建议：财务证明
定要早准备，因为有时候银会让你冻结部分资产去开这个财务证明，所以定定要早准备。
这期间Xinxin师也直在催我填表，跟我讨论把什么样的活动放在表单上更合适，真的是常常负责，我也好喜欢。
https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/PSH0Axr9zkjMX7IsXbfJxA 3/12
https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/PSH0Axr9zkjMX7IsXbfJxA 4/12
Alice创作的科普漫画
04：早点规划，少点迷茫
关于学申请还有很重要的点就是在迷茫中学会找寻真正的我。那时候我还特别的天真，觉得哎呀学申请12年级准备就可以了，
11年级其实不担太多，但其实不是，定要早准备！定要早准备！我也希望学弟学妹们在申请的时候早开始，然后在迷茫期的时
候能遇到帮助他们，引导向的。
还有点建议就是稳住态。因为我在签约浑朴之前其实是属于那种较嚣张的好学，就是我觉得只要成绩好就会有好学会录取
我，但其实并不是那样的。你不光要成绩好，你还要去做其他的很多的事情来表达你对社会这个世界的关，并且你还要在书中体现
出那点，所以我觉得在这个上有引导还是较重要的。

早晚都刷题，个来说我觉得题海战术常有，因为它们让你基本上熟悉下题型并且增加下的信，且你可以从错题中
学到很多很多东。
年少轻狂的我当时对于标化并不是多么的重视，因为上届达到1500的学学姐常多，所以我以为1500就很容易，但其实并不是。
所以如果你的孩现在是九年级或者年级就开始准备就可以了，不要等到年级再去开始。
幸亏我遇了浑朴要不然我真的不知道我的申请会是什么样，可能就不会去做学术活动，也不会去做其他的那些课外活动，书可能
也不会被可爱的Mark改的这么好。因此，早点找申请机构可以从很早开始规划，这样你在呈现给学招官的活动表中就是有种统
性，这样就会显得更可信点，然后学招官会更喜欢点。
https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/PSH0Axr9zkjMX7IsXbfJxA 5/12
当你真正理清的迷茫并且在书中呈现出来时，这就可以让书显得常的真诚，因为你确实是经历过这样的段迷茫的时
期，招官也希望看到你在其中得到了成。我身边很多分享的时候都很少谈及 迷茫 这个问题，但我觉得其实它常的重要，你需要
从对很浅的理解去真正的深层理解，并且搞清楚想要什么，的标是什么，如何看待和这个世界。
05：找对最有的朋友
我在遇浑朴之前常常的迷茫，因为我完全不知道的专业向是什么，也完全不知道可以做什么活动，对于学申请毫
了解毫头绪。对于我的迷茫缓解最的也就是书师吧，因为我们经常会谈起些较深的话题，让我去真正地客观地去看待
以及思考我过去的些事情。
Alice喜爱阅读的书籍
我有次跟Mark打电话谈论书的时候聊着聊着扯远了，就聊到本书上去，然后他跟我说我给你推荐本书，巧合的是我也看过这本
书，并且特别喜欢，我就跟他说：啊！你也喜欢这本书！

content:
书籍我有次跟Mark打电话谈论书的时候聊着聊着扯远了，就聊到本书上去，然后他跟我说我给你推荐本书，巧合的是我也看过这本书，并且特别喜欢，我就跟他说：啊！你也喜欢这本书！
总之和Mark聊天更像是和朋友的种聊天，但是这个朋友不光是你的朋友，且还对你帮助的常，导师的般存在。让感觉他们
不光只是你的留学机构，是个真正的想去帮你、真正想要去倾听你故事的。
06：给家朋友的点建议
对于家朋友，（我其实也没有资格说家应该怎么怎么做，毕竟我没有做过家）我认为家对于孩的引导和教育真的是太重要
啦！我的直对于我就是较宽松的那种，他们也不太关我的在校成绩，从就不太关，但是他们直就是在原则上保持着严
肃，所以我觉得家必须要给孩做好个典范，然后在孩很迷茫的时候能对他们进安慰和引导不是斥责。
如，我身边其实有很多同学他们都是在申请季的时候因为家的些施压导致他们更加的迷茫，最后申请结果不理想，但其实他们
本来都有能申上好的学校，却因为家庭原因给分了。
就我个，我在我爸爸妈妈这样的环境和教育下成的常快乐，然后也懂得做些决定不是只是依赖于外界对于我的要
求。

【浑朴酷孩】2019er－Jerry的故事（范德堡学ED）
朴朴君 浑朴Catalyst 2018-12-28
引
浑朴2019er 岛Jerry同学是辗转通过个知道我们的。作为今年范德堡Peabody教育学院（全美排名第三的教育学院）在中国境内录取的
唯学， Jerry受到了整个岛市留学业的关注。 他的阳光和幽默也感染了浑朴的每员，很荣幸能把这位率真可爱的北男孩的故事分
享给家：
（下以第称叙述）
https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/A6trAhCSXiERe0xq9tL41Q 1/6
序
早上七点，刺的闹铃把我吵醒，习惯性地拿起床头的机，朦胧着眼就翻阅起邮箱。告，告，还是告。忽然，Vanderbilt
Undergraduate Admission 的名映眼帘，吓得我把机甩到了地上。停顿了分钟，我才意识到不是今天放榜，于是顺把机捡起来，
点开了邮件：录取结果将会在中国时间四公布。
四早上七点，夜没睡好，竟然点可以暗示我录取结果的梦都没有做，不免叹了，洗漱洗漱，就去上学。
早上九点，集了向善，好运常伴和思聪超越，合体做法的表情包和学校最爱哭的助教作为护法，我毅然决然的打开了Vanderbilt
Portal：Dear Yufei, Congratulations! You have been admitted to the first-year class entering Peabody College at Vanderbilt
University for fall 2019.
第章
转眼到了11年纪，标化成绩进展还算顺利，但掐指算，还差个中介助我臂之。在选择中介上，我们是常谨慎的，在考察了国内部分
机构后，还是法做出选择。直到意间和学学姐们交流的时候听说了上海浑朴教育，且他们对浑朴的评价常，说是很靠谱很良的中
介，于是我们也决定探究竟。
https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/A6trAhCSXiERe0xq9tL41Q 2/6
还记得是个星期的早上，还没等我准备好，准时的板Yicen就给我打来了电话。我接起电话后，听到的是个温柔的学的声，和我想

我们也决定探究竟。https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/A6trAhCSXiERe0xq9tL41Q 2/6还记得是个星期的早上，还没等我准备好，准时的板Yicen就给我打来了电话。我接起电话后，听到的是个温柔的学的声，和我想
象中的胡渣男形成了强烈的对。在和Yicen简单介绍了的各项成绩，爱好，和课外活动后，Yicen他那福尔摩斯般的洞察，找出了我身
上那些常独特的点，并且进步放，将我描绘成个关少年理教育的美式脱秀演员。沉浸在美好的幻想中，我也深知脚踏实地的
重要性，并且充满了信与希望。
第章
在18年的22号，我们终于找到了个机会去上海和浑朴。说实话，当时我可激动了，先我的个故事终于有着落了，其次我终于可以
到我想象中的胡渣男了。下了机后，先我感受了下上海的感觉，结果发现和岛没差多少，除了多点…因为预计程只有天，
所以我们还没来得及吃午饭，就直奔浑朴本营。在路上，我惊奇地发现浑朴办公室就坐落在上海市中，被数条吃街所包围，这好感度
下就提了上来，毕竟以后过来写书的时候，可以吃个遍了。
穿过条街，进办公楼，找到正确的楼层，我们终于抵达了浑朴办公室。我们进后的第感受就是，这中介真是低调奢华有内涵。和普通中
介那种申请结果和锦旗挂满墙，怕你看不到的嗨，浑朴真是股清流。他的内饰常简单，但是个沙发和coffee bar的存在让我感到了家
的感觉。当时Yicen，Jack, Chris, Charles 都在，他们每个都热情的和我们打招呼聊天。
坐进了Yicen的办公室，虽然有些紧凑，但是常整洁。当然，Yicen得还挺帅的，不是胡渣男。因为和Yicen之前的很多次交流，我们这次

Chris, Charles 都在，他们每个都热情的和我们打招呼聊天。坐进了Yicen的办公室，虽然有些紧凑，但是常整洁。当然，Yicen得还挺帅的，不是胡渣男。因为和Yicen之前的很多次交流，我们这次
直接切正题，开始计划接下来的升学作：夏校申请，阅读理书籍，继续公益活动，开始书写作，以及塑造stand-up comedian这个形
象。
在将近三个时的深沟通后，我们都分满意，更重要的是，我充满了信。我们都认为浑朴团队是我们遇到的最靠谱的中介，于是我们毫不
犹豫的签约了。临前，跟每个都道了别，我的浑朴故事也正式拉开了序幕。

在六五到七期间，我再次来到了上海浑朴作室，准备这为数不多的时间进头脑暴，书创作，以及最重要的，尝试成为
个stand-up comedian。
在上海settle down以后，我的第件事当然是！去绍兴吃了个斩鸡，还有个店的鸭粉丝汤不错，还有鳝丝!那个最好吃了！（这就是
去浑朴的好处）
Back to the topic…
从周到周，我会点去到公司，然后跟Chris头脑暴每个书的主题，找出相同点和不同点，然后思考身的哪个故事或者特点可以去
限扩。来到浑朴之前，我真的觉得书头脑暴点处都没有，直到我拿到那些特别抽象并且宽泛的题以后，我才终于意识到了和专家
起头脑暴的重要性。在这个过程中，Chris直在为我拓展思路，并且认真记录我所说的每点细节，然后帮我找到其中的逻辑性。有了
Chris的帮助，我的书进展分顺利，可以说是特别顺利。在那个周，我乎完成了部分书的初稿。
除了写书，Charles还在同时为我做着试辅导，因为不管是on-campus interview 还是 InitialView都对申请美国名校关重要。在和
Charles的每次谈，Charles都能为我提出宝贵意。在他的帮助下，我的on-campus interview可以说是常成功，InitialView也是次通
过。
Yicen对我的帮助也是很，毕竟他是我的定期骚扰对象。特别是在申请策略上，他帮了我很的忙。我之前直对康奈尔情有独钟，毕竟他
是ED热，且对中国学的录取数也是相当可观。可是在Yicen对我的连番打击轰炸以后，我认识到了地理劣势以及的平有限，于是
果断放弃康奈尔，然后追求范德堡的Peabody College （跟我的专业以及活动分匹配）。
在上海的个周，April不仅辅导我填写各式各样的申请站，她还是我们的后勤部，带我吃遍旁边那条街。

https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/A6trAhCSXiERe0xq9tL41Q 3/6
离开上海后，我紧接着参加了康奈尔的三周夏校和Pioneer Research Program。其中令我印象最为深刻的，便是Pioneer。在这个项中，你可
以和全世界各地的相互交流，并且跟随个教授，在你喜欢的领域中完成篇学平的论。在这个项中，我取得了较好的成绩，也和同
学教授收获了友谊。更重要的是，Pioneer整体幅提升了我的学术背景。现在想起来，真的很感谢浑朴给我介绍了这个质量项。
2018年最繁忙的夏天结束后，我就直接回到了岛，开始我申请阶段的最后冲刺。经过个夏天的努加班，现在的我还算轻松，可以有序按时
的完成所有Chris给我的作业。在章遍遍的修改中，Chris有深度的评语总是可以让我看到新的突破。还记得在最后，每当我收到Chris
发给我的finalized version，我都常满意。当然在收到最终版本后，我还会检查遍，保证所有信息是正确的。在提交完ED Vandy申请

在我的留学故事以及活中，stand-up comedy可以说是常重要的环。它不仅带给了我学申请中的独特性，且丰富了我的活。
（Jerry在现场表演脱秀）
在10年纪的时候，我就迷上了脱秀，每天都会花上两个时浏览YouTube上的Conan OBrien, Jimmy Kimmel. Jimmy Fallon, James
Corden, etc. 在笑的同时，我也开始在学校尝试搞的脱秀节，可惜好景不，因为脱秀在中国并不是常普及。于是在和Yicen的
交谈中，他推荐给我了Stand-up Comedy这个思路。因为之前的各种表演和演说基础，我并不是很怯场，且很快就掌握了这项爱好。说实话
我的第次公开表演本应该是在上海个常有名的喜剧俱乐部，Yicen帮我联系了场次，并且找了同是脱秀演员的他的朋友给了我些指
导。但是到我上去说的时候，我忽然就害怕了，然后就退出了。后来想起来，真的是很后悔，但更多的是可惜，毕竟还是要尝试下的。于是在
我们学校的开幕式，在Yicen的励下，我开始了的英单相声涯。尝到了甜头，后来是发不可收拾，我参加了各种各样的喜剧
节，去拓展的圈。当我明年去了美国，我还是会坚持下去这个爱好，我坚信这将会为我提供限机遇。
终章
过了年，就是我在浑朴度过的整整年了。在这说不说短不短的年，认识了最靠谱的中介，最棒的mentors，和最好的朋友们。与其说
浑朴只是家升学机构，不如说他更是个家庭。在这个家庭，我们互相学习，互相进步，都做出了最令骄傲的成绩。我为你们感到骄
傲，也为感到豪。

Course Codes: HS5111 (SL Y1); HS5121 (SL Y2); HS5131 (HL Y1); HS5141 (HL Y2)
Duration: Two years
Prerequisites: Spanish 3, Spanish 4, Accelerated Intermediate Spanish as a
prerequisite (for SL only) or teacher recommendation
Credits: 2.0
Spanish B is a language acquisition course designed for students
with some previous experience of the target language. In the lan-
guage B course, students further develop their ability to communi-
cate in Spanish through the study of language, themes and texts.
In doing so, they also develop conceptual understandings of how
language works and international-mindedness through the study of
the Spanish language and Hispanic cultures. At both levels of lan-
guage B (SL and HL), students learn to communicate in Spanish in
familiar and unfamiliar contexts. They describe situations, narrate
events, explain problems and support their personal opinions for
a variety of purposes and on a variety of topics related to the five
prescribed themes: Identities, Experience, Human ingenuity, Social
organization and Sharing the planet. Spanish B provides students
with a basis for further study, work and leisure through the use of
an additional language. Students will be assessed regularly with
quizzes and tests, reading and listening comprehension tasks, as
well as individual written and oral productions. At the end of the
second year, students will sit the externally assessed IB exams.
Higher Level Coursework: The study of two literary works
originally written in Spanish. The distinction between language
B SL and HL can also be seen in the level of competency the
student is expected to develop in the receptive, productive and
interactive skills.

The SAS Chinese Program
The goal of the Chinese program is to enable students to
advocate for self, others and ideas in Chinese in a way that
fosters collaboration, enhances global citizenship, challenges
established thought, and leads to creative ideas. The SAS Chi-
nese program marks progress toward achievement of this goal
through ACTFL standards.
Oral Language
The ability to communicate in oral language is measured
through assessments rooted in the Oral Proficiency Interview
(OPI) by ACTFL. The OPI measures the language proficiency
needed to ensure work readiness for differing types of employ-
ment. The OPI assessment measures from Novice (emerging
levels of language for a young child or second language learn-
er) to Superior (proficiency that provides a linguistic base for
success in careers such as that of a judge, philosopher, or dip-
lomat). The SAS measure of oral language proficiency ranges
from Novice to Advanced High. Advanced High includes most
aspects of the Superior range skills of the OPI.
Literacy
Reading comprehension for class placement is measured
through Level Chinese assessments. Level Chinese offers
assessment as well as support for reading from Level C, a very
basic text of foundational literacy to Level T, which provides
the foundation for Advanced High levels of courses as well as
for the IB Language A courses. Writing samples are analyzed
by teachers. Writing levels range from entrance to the Novice
course, in which students will begin to understand how charac-
ters are formed to the Advanced High course in which students
narrate and persuade with organized, precise and artistically
written language.
Placement
Students are placed in courses that best represent their skill
set and next steps for learning in accordance with standards.
The High School program at SAS offers seven levels of Chi-
nese. The SAS course names reflect the ACTFL exit standard of
the course.

Physical computing refers to the creation of devices that utilize
electronics, mechanical components and computer logic to sense
and respond to the surrounding world. This year-long course is
designed around hands-on activities and projects that challenge

physical performance and provides the opportunity to apply these

include further anatomy; the endocrine system; fatigue; friction
and drag; skill acquisition and analysis; genetics and athletic per-
formance, and exercise and immunity.

The mission of Global Online Academy (GOA) is to reimagine learning
to enable students to thrive in a globally networked society.
GOA provides a positive, interactive, and academically rigorous envi-
ronment for students to learn. We offer courses that connect students
to topics they care about, and we offer a network that connects stu-
dents to peers as passionate as they are.
As GOA learners, our students also develop a specific set of skills,
skills that might not be exercised as often in a bricks-and-mortar envi-
ronment. Based on our research, student surveys, and feed- back from
our faculty, we have identified the following six core competencies
that our students develop in practical, hands-on ways, no matter which GOA course they take:

Welcome to
Virtual High School
Global Consortium
SAS students in grades 11 and 12 may request to take an online course from the Virtual High School (VHS) for SAS credit. These courses will
be taken entirely online from a non-SAS teacher. Courses offered by VHS include AP and regular courses. Many VHS courses are offered
for one semester while AP classes are offered for a full year. You can peruse the courses available in the VHS Course Catalog at http://www.
govhs.org/Pages/Academics-Catalog.
SAS students may take a maximum of seven courses in any semester, which can include one VHS course per semester. The grade for the VHS
course will appear on the students SAS report card and transcript and will be calculated as part of their grade point average. There is no
additional cost for an approved SAS student to take a VHS course.
Students who are interested in taking a VHS course should review all the relevant information on the Virtual High School site and complete
the VHS Pre-Student Survey (http://www.govhs.org/Content/InfoFor-StudentSurvey) to decide if an online course is right for them. Students
should then meet with their guidance counselor to discuss the implications of taking a VHS course.
Students who, after meeting with their counselor, would like to request to take an online VHS course should complete the VHS application
form (available in the Counseling Office) and attach a copy of the VHS Pre-Student Survey with their answers. The completed application
should be submitted to the students counselor with their course selection form at the regular due date for course selections.
Seats for VHS courses are limited. Mr. Tracie Dotson, Puxi HS VHS site coordinator, will make the final approval for all VHS course requests.
Priority for VHS courses will be given to students with schedule conflicts.
If you are interested in taking an online course, please review the VHS Course Catalog (http://www.govhs.org/Pages/Academics-Catalog)
and carefully decide which courses you might like to take. If you have any questions about the VHS program at SAS, please contact your
counselor.

SAS students in grades 11 and 12 may request to take an online course from the Virtual High School (VHS) for SAS credit. These courses
will be taken entirely online from a non-SAS teacher. Courses offered by VHS include AP and regular courses. Many VHS courses are of-
fered for one semester while others are offered for a full year. You can peruse the courses available in the VHS Course Catalog at https://
my.vhslearning.org/PublicStudentCourseList.aspx.
SAS students may take a maximum of seven courses in any semester, including a VHS course. The grade for the VHS course will appear on
the students SAS report card and transcript and will be calculated as part of their grade point average. There is no additional cost for an
approved SAS student to take a VHS course.
Students who are interested in taking a VHS course should review all the relevant information on the Virtual High School site and com-
plete the VHS Pre-Student Survey to decide if an online course is right for them. Students should then meet with their counselor to discuss
the implications of taking a VHS course.
Students who, after meeting with their counselor, would like to request to take an online VHS course should complete the VHS application
form (available in the Counseling Office) and attach a copy of the VHS Pre-Student Survey with their answers. The com- pleted application
should be submitted to the students counselor with their course selection form at the regular due date for course selections.
Seats for VHS courses are limited. Students will be informed whether or not their request has been approved later in the spring. Priority
for VHS courses will be given to students with schedule conflicts and students who are requesting courses not offered at SAS.
If you are interested in taking an online course, please review the VHS Course Catalog (http://www.govhs.org/Pages/Academics- Catalog)
and carefully decide which courses you might like to take. If you have any questions about the VHS program at SAS, please Contact your
counselor.

are responsible for reimbursing the school for the cost of the course.

The Innovation Institute is a transformational approach to education in which students are empowered to solve real-world problems
through collaborative and creative processes. The Institute places learners at the center of the educational experience and challenges
them to think critically and apply their learning to complex, interdisciplinary tasks. Students are asked to stretch themselves beyond the
traditional learning framework by engaging in Project Based Learning that requires the use of 21st century skills.
2021-2022 was the inaugural year for The Innovation Institute at SAS Pudong. Current Innovation Institute ninth graders will continue into
the tenth grade Inno program. Eighth grade families will be invited to apply to participate in the spring. Qualifying applications will be
placed in a lottery to determine the makeup of the first ninth grade cohort. Cohorts will range from 20-30 students in size at first, and will
be required to complete the two-year sequence of Innovation courses. The first cohort will complete its tenth grade experience in 2022-2023.
The Innovation Institute is founded on four core principles.

The first cohort will complete its tenth grade experience in 2022-2023.The Innovation Institute is founded on four core principles.
1. Provide a 21st century learning environment where students actively apply the skills of communication, collaboration, creativity, and
critical thinking.
2. Integrate core academic disciplines so that students explore learning concepts by making connections across academic domains.
3. Incorporate relevant, real-life situations through effective implementation of project-based learning.
4. Ensure that interdisciplinary project-based learning is rigorous, and all students taking a specific course will receive instruction
driven by the same SAS standards.
Participation in the Innovation Institute requires a two-year com- mitment. Institute students in grade 9 and 10 are a part of a small learn-
ing community with four teachers who collaborate closely in order to provide an integrated learning experience.

What differentiates the Innovation Institute from the core program? The curriculum is taught through shared themes and projects that
connect all four Institute courses, which allows students to explore the topics in an applied, real-world manner. During projects, students
engage in design thinking processes and receive feedback from experts. Students are assessed through traditional assessments such as
quizzes, exams, and essays; however, they will also be asked to apply their learning through collaborative projects that address real-world
issues. For more information about the Innovation Institute please contact Dr. Benjamin Lee at benjamin.lee@saschina.org

Graphic Design
Course Code: 8010
Prerequisites: Open to grade 9 to 12 students
In this class students explore visual communication as it applies to
the commercial art of Graphic Design. They learn about the prin-
ciples of design, how these can be manipulated to improve design
work, how designs differ depending on their intended target audi-
ence and about the various career paths in Graphic Design.
They will learn how to work in both raster and vector graphics
through projects such as book illustration, menu, logo, signage and
poster design. We will explore design processes including visual
research, thumbnailing ideas, creating mock-ups, pitching and pre-
senting design proposals, through to realizing completed designs.
This course leans heavily towards working digitally, with some
sketchbook work in traditional media.

ing design, industrial sign design, illustration and poster design.

Please review the information below. Teachers and counselors provide guidance and support to students throughout this process. We
encourage students to ask questions, seek advice, and engage in dialogue with us as they consider their options.
Course Catalog
The Course Catalog is available for download from http://www.saschina.org/en/academics/high-school. The catalog includes descriptions,
course codes, and prerequisites. Every departments courses are also represented by a flowchart that provides a snapshot of how each de-
partments courses are sequenced. Students need to reference the course catalog in order to complete their course selection form. Some
courses listed in the course catalog may not be offered if there is limited or no student interest. This may vary from year to year depending
on student preference.
Course Preference Form
Students will receive a paper copy of the course preference form at the course preference meetings in January. All students will meet with
their counselor and speak with their teachers about their course preferences as well as request their signatures to indicate the strength of
their recommendation.
Signatures and Recommendations
After students receive their teachers signatures, parents need to review their childs course preference form, discuss the choices with
their child, and sign the form. Counselors are available to answer questions and meet with families to discuss options. The last stop a stu-
dent makes is to the counselor. The counselor reviews and discusses the course preference form including the overall load or rigor,
and the students request to enroll in a course against a teachers recommendation.
Override/Overload
If students are considering a course they have not been recommended by a teacher or counselor to take, they must complete the Course
Override/Overload Form. In addition, overrides and overloads will require a parent(s) appointment with the counselor, or in lieu of a face-
to-face appointment a phone conversation, to ensure the parent(s) have full understanding of the override/overload process. These appoint-
ments will take place prior to students inputting their preferences on PowerSchool.
IB/AP Exam Fees
Please be aware that any appropriate IB/AP testing fees will be applied to student accounts in November at the same time as tuition for
second semester. These fees are separate from and in addition to regular SAS tuition fees.
Schedule Changes
Please read the schools policy regarding schedule changes (in the student handbook). This policy will be reviewed with students at the
course preferences meetings by the students counselors.
Scheduling is a process that takes months to complete and involves matching teaching staff to student demand for courses. Teaching
schedules, classroom space, and student interest are only a few of the considerations when the high school master schedule is built. The
driving force behind this process is the information students submit on their course preference forms. Teachers and counselors are available
to advise students on finding the best fit and balance. The completed form should represent a students thoughtful and informed choices.
Students must understand that limited movement is permitted in their schedules after they have submitted their course preference forms
to their counselor. Students and parents may not request to have specific teachers or classes with friends. All course requests are final
unless the placement is clearly inappropriate or there is a conflict with another course. In this case, counselors will contact students and
advise them on other course options.
Requests to add, delete, or change a course must be made to the students counselor before the end of the first ten days of the semes-
ter. Students must complete a Schedule Change Request form that can be picked up at the counselors office. All efforts will be made to
schedule students with their preferred courses, if however there is a conflict or a course is already filled, counselors will contact students
and advise them of their other course options.

Student
Handbook
2021-2022
The Frederick Gunn School
99 Green Hill Road
Washington, CT 06793-1200
www.frederickgunn.org
School Code  070825
Head of School - Peter Becker

In 1850 Frederick Gunn established a school basedon the belief that
strength of character was the goal of education. Today,The Frederick
Gunn School rests on the four cornerstones of character:scholarship,
integrity, respect and responsibility. Character isforged in a cohesive,
diverse community informed by a challenging collegepreparatory
curriculum, a broad range of athletic, artistic andsocial activities and
a faculty of scholars and committed educators dedicatedto the
intellectual and ethical development of every student.A Frederick
Gunn School graduate is a broadly educated, sociallyresponsible
citizen with tested beliefs, strength of characterand the courage to
act on convictions.

This Handbook has been prepared as a source of referencefor all
members of the school. We are a community sharingfacilities among
faculty, students, staff, and administration, andthe information within
this Handbook will help us to live, learn, and worktogether. Students
and families are encouraged to ask questions and torefer to our
website and to HighlanderNation for additional information,as this
Handbook cannot address every possible issue thatmay arise.
The rules and regulations set forth in this Handbookare binding at
all times while a student is under our jurisdiction,including
school-sponsored trips, travel to and from The FrederickGunn
School, and during school vacations when school isin session (both
on- and off-campus).Rules may be subject to somechange during
the course of the school year with prior formal communication.

THE FREDERICK GUNN SCHOOL is named in honor of itsfounder,
Frederick William Gunn, an outdoorsman and naturalistrecognized as
the founder of recreational camping in the UnitedStates, a
courageous abolitionist, leader of the UndergroundRailroad in
Washington, Connecticut, and a pioneering educator.After graduating
from Yale University and teaching locally in Washingtonand in
Pennsylvania, Mr. Gunn founded his school in 1850on the site of what
The Frederick Gunn School Student Handbook2
is now Gunn Dormitory. As an educational reformer and an
abolitionist, Mr. Gunn modeled both resilience inthe face of
unanticipated challenges and a willingness to standup for the rights
of all people. His school welcomed boys and girls,students black and
white, as well as international students, in defianceof social norms. For
171 years, our educational philosophy has been inspiredby Mr. Gunns
belief that strength of character is the goal of education.The school
today continues to honor his vision and ideals bypreparing students
to make a difference in the lives of others, to putcitizenship into action
and be a force for good.
Mr. Gunn has been succeeded by 10 Heads of School:John Chapin
Brinsmade, 1881-1922; W. Hamilton Gibson II, 1922-1936;Tertius van
Dyke, 1936-1942; Russell Sturgis Bartlett, 1942-1945;Ogden D. Miller,
1946-1969; C. Burgess Ayres, 1969-1977; David P. Kern,1977-1979;
Michael N. Eanes, 1979-1991; Susan G. Graham, 1991-2012,and Peter
Becker, 2012-present.
The school, under the name of The Frederick Gunn School,Inc., is a
non-profit Connecticut corporation operated by a Boardof Trustees,
of which 14 are Frederick Gunn School graduates. TheFrederick Gunn
School is accredited by the New England Associationof Schools and
Colleges and by the Connecticut Association of IndependentSchools
(CAIS) and is approved by the Connecticut State Departmentof
Education. The Frederick Gunn School is a member ofThe Association
of Boarding Schools, A Better Chance, Inc., the Associationof Business
Officers of Preparatory Schools, American SecondarySchools for
International Students and Teachers, Inc., the Associationof College
Counselors in Independent Schools, the Business OfficersAssociation
of Housatonic Schools, the College Board, CAIS, theNational Science
Teaching Association, the Cum Laude Society, the NationalAssociation
for College Admission Counseling, the National Associationof
Independent Schools, the New England Association forCollege
Admission Counseling, the New England Associationof Schools and
Colleges, the Secondary School Admissions Test Board,and the School
Scholarship Service.
The Frederick Gunn School Student Handbook3

Important Information
Breakfast Check-In
Dining Hall Hours
The Frederick Gunn School Student Handbook4

Mr. Gunn believed honor to be a primary requisiteof character. At The
Frederick Gunn School, we believe a sense of honormust be the
foundation of a healthy community. Each student musttake
responsibility for honorable conduct as a consciousand chosen way
of life.
Students here participate actively in much of thestudent-related
governance and in some important aspects of the decision-making
process of the school and, in return, must merit thetrust and
responsibility placed upon them. The Honor Code infusesall personal
conduct.

The Frederick Gunn School believes that students enrollwith a sincere
desire to learn and a willingness to adhere to theprecepts of the
school. Seriousness of purpose, honesty, and respectfor others and
their property are expected. The faculty serve asmentors,
encouraging the students to accept responsibility,promote the
interests of the school, and experience a personalsense of freedom
within reasonable boundaries established for the commongood.
The Frederick Gunn School embraces a social honorcode and uses
the code actively to determine various freedoms allowedto students.
Respect for others - in the classroom, on athleticfields, in
dormitories, in the dining hall, in the library, inthe student
center, and at school meetings - is a fundamentaltenet of a
school.
In the classroom, students are expected to be attentive,
inquisitive, supportive, and polite  actions shouldbe
conducive to a learning environment.
In interscholastic athletic competitions and in practice
sessions, team members and supporters are expectedto
commit to effort and fair and honorable play. Disrespectfulor
inappropriate language or gestures or acts, or anyplay outside
of the rules, is unacceptable.
In the dormitory and in broader social contexts, studentsmust
be mindful of others rights to privacy, of sharingof facilities, of
The Frederick Gunn School Student Handbook5
appropriate language, and of respect for possessions and
property and persons. Living in harmony with studentsfrom
other cultures and backgrounds constitutes a dimensionof
ones education.
In the dining hall  a place for fellowship and sharing proper
etiquette and courtesy is expected toward staff andother
diners. Appropriate dress as suitable for a meal isrequired.
Cheerful disposition toward helping when asked, andcleaning
up after oneself, is a responsibility.
In the library, all patrons should endeavor to maintainan
environment suitable for quiet study and reflection.Library
materials are to be treated with care and signed outproperly.
The Frederick Gunn School sits as part of a largerglobal
community. As such every student should follow thesocial
honor code both inside and outside our community.Being a
member of this community comes with the expectationthat
we are all stewards of the environment.
It is the responsibility of every member in our community
staff, students, and parents  to promote the socialhonor code
and to address improprieties in a reasonable manner.

For more information regarding diploma requirementsand course
offerings please see the Academics section on ourwebpage.

The Frederick Gunn School operates under a strictinterpretation of an
honor code especially applicable to academics. Everystudent is
required to write out and then sign the followingpledge: I have
neither given nor received improper aid in the preparationof this
assignment. Unless properly attributed to others,it represents
exclusively my own work.
The Frederick Gunn School believes a crucial dimensionof education
is honesty and the independent process of discoveryand
self-actualization.Practically and academically,if you, as a student,
compose an essay using anothers wordsor ideas, ifyou permit
someone to do your homework, if you copy someone elsesnotes for
The Frederick Gunn School Student Handbook6
a take-home test, if you collaborate without permission or without
stating so, you are not learning and you are gainingunfairly through
the efforts of others.These are forms of academicdishonesty and
violations of the Academic Honor Code. The use ofanother students
papers, tests, or notes from this year or a previousyear is also
forbidden and subject to discipline. Collaborationon homework is not
permitted unless authorized or requested in advanceby the instructor
and properly noted.
If there are any questions or concerns while writinga paper, a student
should consult a teacher or advisor or the Academicoffice.

metadata.parent_section: ACADEMIC HONOR CODE AND THE PLEDGE

content:
Academic dishonesty is taken very seriously at TheFrederick Gunn
School. Violations of the Academic Honor Code areconsidered
probation-level disciplinary offenses. These violationsinclude but are
not limited to, purchasing/using a paper written bysomeone else,
plagiarism, cheating off another student in class,taking or giving
another student work, or use of study aids/unauthorizedmaterials in
an assessment.
Students who are found plagiarizing (improper useof quotations,
citations, or works cited) for the first time maynot be placed on
Probation, though in some cases of plagiarism a studentwill be
placed on Probation on their first offense, as determinedby the
Academic office. Students will instead be issued aformal warning
from the Academic office, receive a 0 (zero) on theassignment and
be required to complete an educational plagiarismModule.
Students found plagiarizing a subsequent time willimmediately be
placed on Probation, complete an additional educationalModule on
academic integrity along with regular discipline procedures.
Students who are found violating the academic honorcode in any
other way will be placed on Probation. The AcademicOffice may
decrease the disciplinary response on rare occasionswhen mitigating
circumstances exist.

Parents are required to make travel plans and reservationsaccording
to the exam schedule posted on HighlanderNation. Studentsmay not
The Frederick Gunn School Student Handbook7
leave the exam period early or rearrange their exams. If a student
makes last minute travel plans, we do not guaranteethat an alternate
exam will be provided. In such cases a student mayearn a 0 (zero) for
an exam.
At the opening of school, your child will receivetheir academic
schedule. Please note the subjects and exam datesso you can begin
to make travel plans early. Students may leave aftertheir last
scheduled exam. At the end of the fall term, the finalexam will be
complete by noon on Friday, November 19, and at theend of the
school year, for freshmen, sophomores, and juniors,this will be Friday ,
June 3 at noon.
In year-long courses where the final exam covers onlythe spring term
material, a senior is exempt from the exam if theyreceive a grade of
80% or better for the spring term. A senior is neverexempt from an
exam in a class with a cumulative final exam (Math10, 20, 21, 29, 30, 32,
Spanish I and II, French I and II, Mandarin I andII), and they must pass
this final exam (at least a 50%) in order to earna diploma.
In a term-long course or a course which assigns atake-home project
or final paper in lieu of an exam any final assessmentexemption will
be at the teachers discretion. The teacher will informany students
who are exempt on the last day of class or the daythe take-home or
final paper assignment is distributed.

The Frederick Gunn School grades on a straight percentagegrading
system. Any grade above 59% is considered a passinggrade. Note,
however, that students failing a cumulative examination(grade below
50%)  despite earlier passing grades  in a sequentialcourse
(Spanish, Mandarin, and French I and II, Algebra I,Geometry, Topics in
Algebra II, Algebra II, and Algebra II Honors) willbe required to repeat
the course either at an accredited summer school,during the
following year, or per a Frederick Gunn approved tutoring/examination
format. Seniors who fail any of these cumulative finalswill receive a
Certificate of Attendance, not a Diploma.
Incompletes may only be granted by the Academic Office.They will be
allowed in cases of illness or similarly extenuatingcircumstances.
The Frederick Gunn School Student Handbook8

The Frederick Gunn School runs on a trimester gradingschedule, with
formal grade communication to families six times ayear. At the fall,
winter, and spring midterms, report cards will includeprogress report
grades and an advisor comment summarizing a studentsacademic
progress and general well-being. End of term reportcards will include
final term grades as well as individual teacher comments.The end of
year report card will include an additional advisorcomment
summarizing a student's progress for the year. OfficialFrederick Gunn
School transcripts will include term grades as wellas yearlong
averages.

A student may be placed on one of three levels ofhonor roll based on
their academic performance, at the end of each term.Students
earning a grade of 80% and above in all courses willbe placed on the
Honor Roll. Students earning a grade of 85% and abovein all courses
will be placed on the High Honor Roll. Students earninga 90% and
above in all courses will be placed on the Dean'sList.

A student on Academic Warning three consecutive termsis required
to confer with the Academic Dean to discuss theirfuture at The
Frederick Gunn School. Academic Warning status isassigned to a
student earning below 60% in a term or earning a gradeof 60% to 64%
in each of two courses.

If a student is scheduled for three tests on a singleday, they are
entitled to have a test rescheduled for another timeif such
rescheduling is done at least a day ahead of time.Students should
pay careful attention to upcoming test dates and planahead to avoid
an overload. A student may enlist the help of theiradvisor or the
Academic Office in establishing a workable new schedulewith the
teachers involved.
The Frederick Gunn School Student Handbook9

Private music/dance lessons are a year-long commitment;students
may not drop private music/dance instruction during the school year.
Private music/dance instruction does not count towardsan Arts credit,
but students are graded for their work, just likeany other class.
Students in Private Instruction take one lesson perweek. Lesson
durations range from 45 to 60 minutes. Lesson feesare billed home
accordingly, based upon an hourly rate. These lessonsare typically
scheduled during the academic day (between 8:00 a.m.and 3:00
p.m). Lessons are scheduled based upon teacher, student,and facility
ability and will be reflected in HighlanderNation.
Parents are billed home for these lessons, whetherthe student attends
the lesson or not.Excused absences (illness, standardizedtests,
family emergency, etc.) need to be called into ext.260 (or emailed to
castonguayr@frederickgunn.org) or the private lessonadjunct
directly, either by email and/or phone as soon asthe student knows
they will be absent. It is not the Health Centersresponsibility to
notify the Performing Arts Department that a studentwill be absent.
It is a students responsibility to contact the musicdepartment
directly.Should the teacher not receive this communicationprior to
their arrival to campus, lessons will be billed homeaccordingly.
Families will be billed for all unexcused absences.Unexcused
absences also result in Commitment Absences, justlike skipping a
regularly blocked class. Students with three or moreunexcused
absences do not receive credit for the course (forthe year).

Attendance is tracked each day and students who missthree
academic classes, private music lessons, co-curricularcommitments,
mandatory performances, School Meetings, or tutorialabsences,
without prior proper permission, will be placed ondiscipline (please
see the Discipline section for further information).These absences are
classified as Unexcused Commitment Absences.
UnexcusedCommitment Absences:
The Frederick Gunn School Student Handbook10
For every 3 Unexcused Commitment Absences in a term
students are required to meet with the DOS. Parents are also
notified. The student is then placed on Status Warning.
For every 5 Unexcused Commitment Absences in a term
students are required to meet with the Academic office,their
advisor, parents (as available), and the DOS office.Student is
then placed on Discipline Warning.
For every 8 Unexcused Commitment Absences in a term
students are again required to meet with the Academicoffice,
their advisor, a Prefect, parents (as available),and the DOS
office. The student is then placed on Probation (pleasesee the
Discipline section for more information regardingProbation).
For every 12 Unexcused Commitment Absences in a term
students will be subject to a meeting with the Deanof Students
and Head of School to determine the students futureat The
Frederick Gunn School. The schools response may bean
immediate Discipline Committee hearing or immediate
dismissal.
ExcusedCommitment Absences (including those who tookTime Off
Campus form(s)):
If a student misses more than 2 of the same commitmentsin a
term, they will be required to meet with DOS or theiradvisor,
depending on the circumstances of the excused absences.
If a student misses more than 4 of the same commitmentsin a
term, they are required to meet with the AcademicOffice and
the Dean of Students Office. The Frederick Gunn Schoolbelieves
that a pattern of excused absences can be detrimentalto a
students learning and to their commitment to ourcommunity.
A sustained pattern of absences may result in a meetingwith
the parents or guardian and in some cases may resultin a
special contract about meeting school obligations.Failure to
meet the conditions of the special contract may leadto
separation from the school.
NOTE: The accumulation of excused and Unexcused Commitment
Absences resets to zero at the beginning of everyterm.
The Frederick Gunn School Student Handbook11

The Frederick Gunn School discourages students from missing
commitments for reasons other than those that arecritical to the
future accomplishments of the student. Attendancein the classroom,
in all co-curricular activities, and all other requiredevents outside of
academic and co-curricular life, is crucial to thesuccess of our
students and our close-knit community. When we failto adhere to
attendance requirements by missing commitments (eventhose with
advance notice), we not only limit our own successes,but we hinder
the successes of our teammates, classmates, and community
members.
If a student makes the decision not to be in attendancefor any
academic, co-curricular (game, meeting, or practice),or school
required commitment, they will need to complete thisTime Off
Campus (TOC) form. This form will need to be completedand
returned to the Dean of Students Office with as muchadvance notice
as possible but no later than 72 hours in advance.The intent of this
form is for the student to engage in conversationto discuss the
reason and possible subsequent effects of the studentsabsence. The
student will meet with the Dean of Students Office,their advisor,
teachers, dorm parents, and co-curricular leaders.This form is not
intended to be used as a free pass to miss commitmentsand should
only be used when absolutely necessary. Student absencesshould be
given with as much notice as possible and this formis preferably
asked to be completed within the first two weeks ofthe term. This
requirement does not apply to medical appointments,as those are
approved and vetted through our Health Center.
The Frederick Gunn School has the ability to denya students request
to miss a commitment. In this instance, the studentmay still choose to
attend their off-campus activity, but will not beexcused from
commitments. As a result, they may face disciplinaryaction according
to the policies outlined in our Student Handbook.
Below are the expectations of students when takinga Time Off
Campus Form:

expect special consideration from their teachers tomake up
for topics or assignments missed for special absences.
